reason: The book is doing exactly what the mandate asks and the regime it was built for is still in force, so the only thing a rewrite would reliably buy me is frictions. NAV is +9.54% against SPY +2.24% with a -3.19% max drawdown, and this leg is nine days old (entered 2026-09-21). The re-tilt toward short-duration cash-flow value in a rate-HIKE regime is being confirmed, not refuted: the 10-year sits at 5.257%, the highest since 2007, the 2-year at 5.163%, core inflation is running 3.3-3.7% against a 2% target, and Governor Barr is still calling for more hikes. October hike odds did soften to 51% from 71% after Williams, but that is a change in pace, not in direction, and nothing in it argues for owning more duration. The mandated inflation-shock hedge is the leg carrying the book: XOM +2.67% and CVX +1.33% with Brent at $102-108 on a live Hormuz closure that Trump refused to negotiate away on 9/28. I deliberately keep that hedge in integrated majors rather than adding to it, because crude is whipsawing 3%+ a day on truce headlines and the majors' refining offsets damp that. The losers are ADBE -7.42% and ACN -6.25%, both long-duration multiple compression in a 5.26% world, but both sit far from their -18% and -15% stops and selling a capitulated quality name seven days and seven percent into a mean-reversion trade is the precise opposite of this strategy's edge. My one genuine complaint is PEP at 7%, a bond-proxy staple the strategy of record claims to have moved away from and which is structurally impaired at these yields; it is -0.84% and rewriting a nine-leg book to fix a 7% leg is negative expected value after 2bps a side plus SEC/TAF. Holding is the active choice here: the thesis is intact, the hedge is paying, and the drawdown is small.
